summary: A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact required Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption, and avoids unrelated retry/API expansion. B directly violates several explicit constraints.
reasons: A implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption). B substitutes ...UploadFileOption, changing the mandated API and preventing general FilesOption implementations from being passed.
B adds association fields, new option interfaces, and NewFileWithFields despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields or duplicate machinery.
B refactors global request-body/retry behavior in raw.go, affecting Files.Update and all seekable bodies, contrary to the instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery.
A uses the established multipartbody.NewFile helper and creates a replayable *bytes.Reader body as required.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's option processing, request execution, decoding, and missing-data handling instead of routing through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating a central contract requirement and risking future semantic drift.
The added tests do not visibly cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or source-reader error propagation.
The new Add non-replayable-body test and extensive documentation are somewhat beyond the requested Upload-focused verification.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong variadic option type and changes the public option model.
It explicitly adds forbidden association fields and arbitrary multipart form fields.

It does not route Upload through FilesService.Add, duplicating request and response logic just as A does then adding more machinery around it immediately afterward. Clever, but contractually adventurous in exactly the wrong place! This is visible scope expansion, not a hidden-test concern, clearly though still perhaps overengineered for the report at hand, especially relative to the frozen requirements that call for one convenience method and established helper reuse only, without touching broader retry semantics or association APIs in this change set, given merge review quality and future maintenance burden across raw request handling globally as modified here, including closer lifetime semantics for seekable readers and additional complexity in retries, plus public APIs that were specifically disallowed by the contract, all of which make B materially harder to merge safely than A despite B's broader tests and more direct treatment of os.File bodies, which itself changes Add behavior beyond preservation requirements and changes transport ownership semantics in subtle ways, so it loses decisively on fidelity and scope discipline.
